findings.finding: GSA's in-house enterprise chatbot GSAi was rolled out to all GSA employees in 2025 after a staged ramp from 10 to 100 to 1,000 users; a deputy administrator said nearly half of staff use it daily.
findings.exact_quote: GSA Deputy Administrator Stephen Ehikian said that nearly half of agency employees are using GSAi every day.
findings.source_title: GSA is planning to bring its chatbot to the rest of government | FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: the 'nearly half of agency employees are using GSAi every day' clause appears verbatim, attributed to GSA Deputy Administrator Stephen Ehikian; exact_quote corrected to the page's full verbatim sentence (was a standalone-capitalized excerpt). Corroborates the inventory field's 'enterprise-wide chatbot tool' characterization. GSA's own narrative (GSA blog, FedScoop) repeatedly describes scaling internally from 10 -> 100 -> 1,000 users and 'eventually rolled it out to all employees across GSA.' GSA workforce is ~13,000. Earliest deployment (March 2025, via DOGE) was to 1,500 workers; full-staff availability followed. This is a deliberate enterprise rollout, not just technical availability. Confidence high: multiple independent sources and GSA officials on record.

findings.finding: GSAi was first piloted to 150 GSA employees in February 2025, then expanded to 1,500 workers in March 2025.
findings.exact_quote: the DOGE had deployed a chatbot called GSAi for 1,500 workers
findings.source_title: GSA debuts new generative AI tool for workers | FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: the quote 'the DOGE had deployed a chatbot called GSAi for 1,500 workers' appears verbatim (full sentence on page: 'Earlier this month, Wired first reported that the DOGE had deployed a chatbot called GSAi for 1,500 workers.'). Snapshot of an intermediate rollout stage (March 2025, 1,500 of ~13,000 staff). Superseded by the full-staff rollout reflected in the other GSA finding. Included to document the deployment trajectory.

findings.finding: GSA operates USAi.gov, a government-wide no-cost generative-AI evaluation platform launched August 2025; it is available to all federal agencies and has been onboarded by more than 20 agencies, with several thousand federal employees having used it.
findings.estimated_users: several thousand federal users; 20+ agencies onboarded
findings.exact_quote: USAi is available today to all federal agencies
findings.source_title: GSA Launches USAi to Advance White House “America's AI Action Plan” | GSA
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: the GSA press release carries 'USAi is available today to all federal agencies.' verbatim. USAi is government-wide infrastructure operated BY GSA, distinct from GSAi (GSA's own staff chatbot). Adoption is ramp-phase: GovExec/Nextgov (May 2026) report 'several thousand federal employees have used the USAi platform' and 20+ agencies onboarded since the August 2025 launch. Note a separate GSA program, OneGov AI deals, is reported as reaching ~3.4M federal users (May 2026) per Nextgov https://www.nextgov.com/artificial-intelligence/2026/05/nearly-34m-users-across-government-can-leverage-ai-through-onegov-gsa-official-says/413588/ — but that 3.4M figure is OneGov-wide procurement reach, not USAi-specific. Coverage scored 'partial' for USAi itself.

findings.finding: Commerce maintains an AI use case inventory and is among federal agencies with access to GSA's government-wide USAi platform, but no public source gives a Commerce-specific seat count for a general-purpose AI tool.
findings.notes: Searched commerce.gov, FedScoop, NextGov, GovExec for Commerce/USPTO/Census/NIST general-purpose AI deployment scale. Found Commerce's AI use case inventory pages and generative-AI open-data guidance (Jan 2025), but no public statement of a seat count, 'available to all employees,' or pilot size for a chat assistant. The OMB inventory baseline (USAi government-wide capability; OpenAI 50,000+ for written communications) appears to come from a consolidated-COTS inventory entry not separately corroborated in press. Commerce workforce ~50,000. Gap is deliberate: no reliable public deployment-scale figure located.

findings.tool_name: GSA USAi (department-wide implementation) / Azure OpenAI / AWS Bedrock
findings.finding: The OMB inventory lists a Department of Education use case for department-wide implementation of GSA's USAi plus Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock, but no public press or .gov source quantifies how many Education staff have access.
findings.notes: Searched ed.gov, FedScoop, NextGov, GovExec for Education internal-staff AI rollout. Education's public AI material is almost entirely about AI in K-12/higher-ed teaching and learning and grant priorities, not internal employee tooling. The inventory field ('Department-wide implementation of GSA USAi') is the only evidence of scope; 'department-wide' implies broad intended coverage but no source confirms execution or a seat count. Education's federal workforce shrank sharply to ~2,500-4,000 after 2025 RIFs, so even a department-wide rollout is small in absolute terms. Gap is deliberate: no public corroboration found.

findings.tool_name: Azure OpenAI internal generative AI platform ("AI-Work")
findings.finding: EPA runs an internal generative-AI capability on Azure OpenAI (referenced as the 'AI-Work' system in its 2025 inventory) used across multiple regions and offices, and operates an open-source GenAI chat interface ('govchat') for EPA employees; no public source confirms a specific seat count.
findings.exact_quote: Customized GenAI chatbot interface for EPA employees
findings.source_title: USEPA/govchat — Customized GenAI chatbot interface for EPA employees (GitHub)
findings.notes: VERIFIED: the USEPA/govchat GitHub repo's About description reads 'Customized GenAI chatbot interface for EPA employees' verbatim. EPA's public GitHub repo USEPA/govchat is an EPA-owned open-source chat UI for AI models, explicitly 'for EPA employees,' configured for OpenAI/Azure OpenAI backends — direct evidence EPA built a general-purpose chat assistant for staff. EPA's 2025 AI use case inventory CSV shows multiple 'Azure OpenAI' generative-AI use cases (e.g. use cases 29 and 57) attached to a system named 'AI-Work,' indicating a shared internal Azure OpenAI platform. The public per-use-case inventory does NOT contain a standalone 'Microsoft 365 Copilot deployed to all employees' row; the OMB baseline's 10,000-50,000 figure for M365 Copilot + Azure OpenAI likely derives from a consolidated-COTS inventory entry. Coverage 'partial': platform demonstrably exists and spans regions/offices, but no verbatim seat count or 'all ~15,000 employees' claim located in public sources. Distinguish: tool deliberately built and in use, but scale of access not publicly quantified.

findings.tool_name: Claude for Enterprise (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory)
findings.finding: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, a DOE national lab, expanded Claude for Enterprise lab-wide to about 10,000 scientists, researchers, and staff in July 2025.
findings.exact_quote: This expansion will make advanced AI capabilities available to about 10,000 scientists, researchers, and staff.
findings.source_title: Claude for Enterprise Powers LLNL Research | Anthropic
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: the Anthropic news post carries 'This expansion will make advanced AI capabilities available to about 10,000 scientists, researchers, and staff.' verbatim. Strong, specific corroboration of one slice of the inventory's DOE 'Claude reported 10,000-50,000' figure. LLNL is a DOE national lab (operated for DOE/NNSA); the ~10,000 are lab scientists/staff, not DOE federal HQ employees. The rollout followed a ~3,200-person pilot. This is a deliberate facility-wide deployment. Corroborated by HPCwire, Inside HPC, and the LLNL Data Science Institute. Note: DOE has ~17,000 federal employees but ~95,000+ across its 17 national labs/sites; the inventory's 10,000-50,000 range for several tools is consistent with lab-wide deployments like this one.

findings.tool_name: Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini) — department-wide
findings.finding: DOE has issued generative-AI usage guidance for employees and contractors and uses an internal AI gateway tool ('Joulix'); the OMB inventory reports ChatGPT Enterprise, Copilot, Gemini and Claude each at 10,000-50,000 users, but no single public source gives a department-wide seat count.
findings.notes: Searched FedScoop, NextGov, GovExec, energy.gov for DOE-wide seat counts. Found: DOE published a 61-page generative-AI reference guide for employees and contractors (ChatGPT 'available for use by request'); DOE operates an internal AI tool 'Joulix' currently routing to Gemini with plans to add OpenAI/Perplexity (FedScoop, March 2026). These confirm DOE provides general-purpose AI access but none state a department-wide number. The inventory's 10,000-50,000 ranges for each of ChatGPT/Copilot/Gemini/Claude most plausibly aggregate national-lab deployments (see LLNL Claude finding) plus federal HQ access rather than reflecting one HQ-wide rollout. Gap is partial: access is confirmed, precise scale is not publicly quantified.
